outputs.exact_statement: Let $X$ be a normal projective $\mathbb Q$-factorial threefold over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>3$. Suppose that $X$ has terminal singularities and that $K_X$ is nef with $\nu(K_X)=1$. Then some positive Cartier multiple of $K_X$ has at least two independent global sections. In particular, $\kappa(X,K_X)=1$ and $K_X$ is semiample.

Suppose that $k$ is uncountable and algebraically closed of characteristic $p>3$, and that $X$ is a projective terminal threefold with $K_X$ nef, $\nu(K_X)=1$, and $n(X,K_X)=3$. There exist a smooth projective threefold $V$, a generically finite separable morphism $\rho:V\to X$, a very ample divisor $H$ on $V$, and a nonzero effective Cartier divisor $$D=\sum_{\alpha}m_\alpha D_\alpha,\qquad
 m_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\qquad \gcd_\alpha m_\alpha=1,$$ with the following properties.*

1.  *The support of $D$ is connected and has simple normal crossings. The divisor $D$ is nef, and $D|_{D_\alpha}$ is numerically trivial for every $\alpha$.*

2.  *There is no $D$-trivial curve through a very general point of $V$. Moreover $D\cdot H^2>0$ and $D^2\cdot H=0$.*

3.  *The invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_D(D)$ is torsion. Its order will be denoted by $r$.*


4.  *For an integer $b\geq0$, an open neighborhood $U$ of $|D|$, and integers $b_\alpha$, there is an isomorphism $$\label{eq:prepared-canonical}
     \omega_V^{\otimes p^b}|_U
     \simeq \mathcal O_U(B_*),\qquad B_*=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha D_\alpha .$$ Consequently $K_V\cdot D\cdot A=0$ for every Cartier divisor $A$ on $V$.

Let $P$ be an excellent normal local surface with closed residue field $l$, and let $g:T\to P$ be a nontrivial projective regular resolution which is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Write $G_i$ for its exceptional integral curves, and take intersection degrees over $l$. Then $G_i^2<0$ for every $i$. More generally, if an exceptional real divisor $Z=\sum_i z_iG_i$ has a positive coefficient, there is an index $j$ with $z_j>0$ and $Z\cdot G_j<0$.
A terminal threefold in the present setting has only isolated singularities.

Let $Y$ be a normal projective threefold over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $L$ be an effective Cartier divisor. Suppose that $L$ is numerically trivial on every integral component of its support and that $\mathcal O_Y(L)|_{L_{\mathrm{red}}\setminus Z}$ is trivial for a finite set of closed points $Z$. Then $\mathcal O_L(L)$ is torsion.

Let $E$ be a semistable torsion-free sheaf. If $F_V^*E$ is unstable and $B$ is its first Harder–Narasimhan term, then the connection induces a nonzero morphism on a big open set $$B\longrightarrow (F_V^*E/B)\otimes\Omega_V^1.$$
If $T_V$ is unstable, its first Harder–Narasimhan term $A$ is closed under Lie brackets and under $p$-th powers of derivations.

Let $A\subset T_V$ be a saturated bracket-closed and $p$-closed subsheaf of rank $d$. There is a finite purely inseparable map $\pi\colon V\to W$ to a normal projective variety, with a factorization $$V\xrightarrow{\pi}W\xrightarrow{\rho}V^{(1)}$$ of relative Frobenius. On open sets whose complements have codimension at least two, the canonical bundles satisfy $$\omega_V\simeq\pi^*\omega_W\otimes(\det A)^{\otimes(p-1)}.
  \label{eq:foliation-canonical}$$

The tangent bundle $T_V$ is strongly semistable for the slope $c_1(-)HD/\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}(-)$. Moreover, $$c_2(V)D\ge0.
  \label{eq:c2-nonnegative}$$
If a line bundle $L$ has $\deg L\le0$, then $h^0(V,L)\le1$.

If $G_1,G_2$ are torsion-free semistable sheaves of slope zero, then $$\dim_k\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(G_1,G_2)\le\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}(G_1)\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}(G_2).
  \label{eq:hom-rank-bound}$$

Let $G$ be a semistable vector bundle of slope zero. For every integer $i$, $$h^0\bigl(V,G(iD)\bigr)\le\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}G,
  \qquad
  h^0\bigl(V,G^{\otimes2}(iD)\bigr)\le(\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}G)^2.
  \label{eq:uniform-bundle-sections}$$ For each fixed bundle $J=G$ or $J=G^{\otimes2}$, the increasing spaces $$H^0\bigl(V,J(iD)/J\bigr),\qquad i=1,2,\ldots,
  \label{eq:polar-part-system}$$ have bounded dimension and eventually stabilize under their natural injections. In particular their elements have a uniform bound on their actual pole orders along every prime component of $D$. This pole bound may depend on $J$; it is uniform in the cut $i$ and in the chosen section.
For every $i>0$, $$H^0\bigl(V,\mathcal O_V(iD)/\mathcal O_V\bigr)=0.$$

The operation $x\mapsto\partial x$ induces maps $$d_s:E_s^{i,a}(E)\longrightarrow E_s^{i-s,a+1}(E)$$ whose cohomology is the next page. At page one, $E_1^{i,a}(E)=H^a(V,P_i^1(E))$; every page has only rows $a=0,1,2$. In particular, with $\delta_s^a(i)=g_s^a(i;E)-g_{s+1}^a(i;E)$ for $a=0,2$, $$\begin{aligned} g_s^0(i;E) &=\dim\mathop{\mathrm{im}}\bigl(H^0(P_i^s(E))\longrightarrow H^0(P_i^1(E))\bigr), \label{eq:bottom-endpoint}\\ g_s^2(i;E)&=g_s^0(1-i;E^!),\label{eq:top-endpoint}\\ g_{s+1}^1(i;E) &=g_s^1(i;E)-\delta_s^0(i+s)-\delta_s^2(i-s). \label{eq:middle-recurrence} \end{aligned}$$ If $M>0$ and $\mathcal O(MD)|_{sD}$ is trivial, the page-$s$ ranks are periodic in $i$ modulo $M$, and $$\label{eq:periodic-euler} \sum_{i\bmod M}\bigl(g_s^0(i;E)-g_s^1(i;E)+g_s^2(i;E)\bigr) =\sum_{i\bmod M}\chi(P_i^1(E)).$$ Finally, at each fixed weight $i$, the stable image in Equation [eq:bottom-endpoint] is precisely the image of the global sections of the completed bundle $\widehat{E(iD)}$ in $H^0(P_i^1(E))$.
There are nonzero leading jets of $\omega_V$ of arbitrarily large width, allowing their upper weight to vary.

Every coefficient of $B_*$ in Equation [eq:canonical-p-power] is divisible by $p^b$. Writing $B_*=p^bB_0$ with $B_0$ integral, there is an isomorphism on the completion along $D$, $$\label{eq:canonical-formal-root} \widehat{\omega}_V\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_V(B_0).$$

Let $G$ be a vector bundle that is semistable of slope zero for the degree $c_1(-)\cdot H\cdot D$. There is a constant $A_G$ such that, for every sufficiently large $e$, $$g^0_{\lfloor c_0M_e\rfloor}(i;G)>0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(i,M_e\mathbb Z)\le A_G.$$

For the prepared data and periods fixed above, let $E$ be a vector bundle on $V$ with the following properties:*

1.  *$\chi(P_i^1(E))=0$ for every integer $i$.*

2.  *For $J=E,E^!$, the spaces $H^0(V,J(nD)/J)$ have dimensions bounded independently of the positive integer $n$.*

3.  *For $J=E,E^!$ there is a constant $A_J$ such that $$g^0_{u_e}(i;J)>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
     \mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(i,M_e\mathbb Z)\le A_J$$ for all sufficiently large $e$.*

*Then global sections of $E_{\mathcal R}$ form a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. Every Laurent Čech $1$-cocycle on a finite affine cover adapted to the bundles and the divisor has an actual Laurent primitive. The same assertion holds after refining such a cover.

On a smooth affine chart with étale coordinates $x_1,x_2,x_3$ and a local equation $f$ for $D$, put $R=\widehat A[1/f]$. The monomials $x^I=x_1^{I_1}x_2^{I_2}x_3^{I_3}$, $0\le I_j<p$, form a basis of $R$ over $R^p$. Ordinary differentials and the Cartier isomorphism extend to this ring. The algebraic bundles $B^1,Z^1$ and their defining exact sequences extend to the corresponding Laurent exact and closed forms, with their Frobenius module structure. In particular, $$\label{eq:cartier-sequences}
 0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_V\longrightarrow F_*\mathcal O_V
   \longrightarrow B^1\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 0\longrightarrow B^1\longrightarrow Z^1
   \xrightarrow{C}\Omega\longrightarrow0$$ are sequences of vector bundles and remain exact on Laurent charts. The images and kernels in the Frobenius de Rham complex are locally free, as are the relevant quotients. Moreover, $$\label{eq:frobenius-duality}
 (F_*\mathcal O_V)^\vee\otimes\omega_V\simeq F_*\omega_V.$$
Every Laurent Čech $1$-cocycle with values in $\Omega$, $B^1$, or $Z^1$ has a Laurent primitive. Global Laurent one-forms form a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space.

Every global Laurent one-form is closed. On the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $$W=H^0(|D|,\Omega^1_{\mathcal R}),$$ Cartier is a bijective inverse-Frobenius-semilinear map, and $C-\mathop{\mathrm{id}}:W\to W$ is surjective as an additive map. Moreover, every additive $\mathcal Z^1$-valued Čech one-cocycle is a coboundary after refining its open cover.
Every $\mathcal R$-line bundle admits an integrable connection whose local connection one-forms are fixed by Cartier.

If $\alpha=\sum_i a_i\,dx_i$ is closed and $C\alpha=\alpha$, then the connection operators $$D_i=\partial_i+a_i:R\longrightarrow R$$ commute and satisfy $$D_i^p=0,
 \qquad [D_i,x_j]=\delta_{ij}.
 \label{eq:horizontal-relations}$$ Here a ring element in an operator formula denotes multiplication by that element.

Let $M$ be a free rank-one $R$-module with a connection whose operators satisfy Equation [eq:horizontal-relations] and commute. Its horizontal module $$H_M=\bigcap_i\ker(D_i:M\to M)$$ is a finite projective rank-one $S$-module, and multiplication gives an isomorphism $$R\otimes_S H_M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }M. \label{eq:horizontal-descent}$$ Formation of $H_M$ commutes with restriction to a smaller Laurent chart retaining the coordinates.

For the smooth affine chart and rings $A,B,R$ above, $B$ is a regular Noetherian ring. Every finite projective rank-one $R$-module extends to a finite projective rank-one $B$-module. Its associated line is locally trivial after restriction to formal Zariski neighborhoods of every point of $U\cap|D|$. The same assertions hold for $B^p\subset R^p$.
Multiplication by $p$ on $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}(|D|,\mathcal R)$ is surjective.
